newsitem.title: FRANCE: Groupe Rivaud companies in buy-out deal.
newsitem.headline: Groupe Rivaud companies in buy-out deal.

text.p: Vincent Bollore, the new chairman of bank Groupe Rivaud, has decided to buy out minority shareholders of a number of Rivaud subsidiaries ahead of a financial clean-up for the losses of airline Air Liberte.

In a statement, three of the Rivaud companies said that following board meetings and after "a first" analysis of possible 1996 provisions for Air Liberte, they had decided to simplify the structure of the companies which hark back to France's colonial past.

Compagnie du Cambodge said it was offering 675 francs per share to the minority shareholders of Mines de Kali Sainte-Therese and 1,400 francs per share to minority holders of Compagnie des Caoutchoucs de Padang.
Cambodge has 49.5 percent of Kali and 36.3 percent of Padang.
The shares had been suspended on the Paris Bourse today. Cambodge closed at 1,115 francs on Wednesday, Kali at 559 francs and Padang at 1,150 francs.
Groupe Rivaud was a main shareholder in airline Air Liberte which went into administration. The bank is also a partner to British Airways Plc in a rescue bid for Liberte.

"The supervisory board members (of the three companies) have decided, unanimously, to start a process of rationalisation of the structures of the various companies of the Rivaud group, which could take place over several years, and has the following aims," the statement said.

"To improve the transparancy of the various legal structures of the group; to define and optimise the activities the group intends to develop; to strenghten the control of the group over its industrial subsidiairies," it added.
It said the bids announced today would increase Rivaud's control while other holders to sell out.

Bollore, also the head of Bollore Technologies, was made chairman of the bank on October 17 after he had become the group's third biggest shareholder behind the founding families represented by Edouard de Ribes and Jean de Baumont.

Rivaud and its two main holding companies, Societe Industrielle et Financiere de l'Artois and Financiere Moncey, form an influential financial constellation in France and are described by newspapers as being close to the ruling RPR Gaullist party.
On October 28, Rivaud's shareholders agreed a capital injection of 800 million francs, partly for Air Liberte.
